findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and recoverable if the underlying storage is compromised or snapshots are exposed.
The snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of the source volume, so sensitive data is stored unencrypted in the snapshot, which can be shared or copied across accounts.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port of the instance to the entire internet, enabling brute-force and unauthorized access attempts.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls (e.g., WAF, load balancer), directly exposing the web server to untrusted networks.

Egress rule allows all traffic (-1 protocol, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which increases risk of data exfiltration if the instance is compromised, violating defense-in-depth network segmentation principles.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet, especially combined with the permissive security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances launched in this subnet, expanding the internet-facing attack surface unnecessarily.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block, risking unauthorized access to network traffic metadata and unencrypted storage of log data.
